text: Working papers in Documents & Reports with Samer Al-Samarrai as an author that deal with education finance:

1. Mobilizing Resources for Education and Improving Spending Effectiveness: Establishing Realistic Benchmarks Based on Past Trends (Policy Research Working Paper WPS8773, 2019-03-11; with Pedro Cerdan-Infantes and Jonathan David Lehe). Global spending trends (about 4.5% of GDP), drivers of spending increases and their link to learning-adjusted years of schooling. http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/244151552329948414

2. Introducing a Performance-Based School Grant in Jakarta: What Do We Know About Its Impact After Two Years? (WPS8223, 2017-10-23). Impact evaluation of a performance component in Jakarta's school grants. http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/826471508762577145

3. Assessing Basic Education Service Delivery in the Philippines: Public Education Expenditure Tracking and Quantitative Service Delivery Study (Working Paper AUS6799, 2016-06-10). Basic education spending rose 60% in real terms 2010-2015. http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/507531468325807323

4. Assessing the Role of the School Operational Grant Program (BOS) in Improving Education Outcomes in Indonesia (Working Paper AUS4133, 2014-12-23). Review of Indonesia's national school grants. http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/779451468253241136
5. Related: Gender Equity and Fee-Free Basic Education in Tanzania (Working Paper 135590, 2019), on the Fee-Free Basic Education Program.

His other working papers in the catalog (Indonesia Economic Quarterly 2015, 'Indonesia - Avoiding the trap' 2014) are not on education finance. His main education finance outputs that are not working papers include Education Finance Watch 2021 (Report 156905), The Role of Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfers in Improving Education Outcomes (2021/2022) and Investing in Human Capital for a Resilient Recovery: The Role of Public Finance (2021).
